newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM says not in alliance talks with BA, AA.
newsitem.headline: KLM says not in alliance talks with BA, AA.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Thursday it was not holding talks with American Airlines and British Airways about joining their planned alliance.
Commenting on a report in De Telegraaf newspaper, KLM spokesman Peter Welhuner said: "The suggestion in the article that talks are being held between airlines about cooperation is not correct."
In the article De Telegraaf quoted American Airlines chairman Bob Crandall as saying he would welcome KLM as a member of the proposed alliance.
"We - American Airlines and also British Airways - would really welcome an alliance with KLM. We have made that quite clear to KLM chairman (Pieter) Bouw," De Telegraaf quoted Crandall as saying.
"We also told him that it was up to KLM to take the initiative," Crandall was further quoted as saying.
Welhuner said Crandall had made no secret of his admiration for KLM.
"Mr Crandall has expressed his admiration for KLM several times in the past and he has done so again," he said.
The KLM spokesman declined to make any further comment on the report in De Telegraaf.
"KLM will not comment on speculation about possible forms of cooperation. If we have anything to communicate in this area, we will do it ourselves, but at the moment we don't," he said.
The media and share dealers have often speculatively linked KLM's name with those of British Airways and American Airlines.
But analysts say KLM's existing link-up with Northwest Airlines would appear to form an obstacle to such a three-way megamerger.
